t64.subject: detect_sret: follow -O0 spilled hidden pointer (stack-slot aliasing)
t64.description:
make_array leaks phantom `a2` (the hidden sret rdi pointer). Two coupled parts; neither safely landable alone (investigated this session).

ROOT CAUSE (trace + IR confirmed): at -O0 the hidden sret pointer rdi(56) is SPILLED to a stack slot then accessed indirectly (reload → struct-fill stores → RETURN). detect_sret's direct-Store(addr=rdi) heuristic sees 0 store_addr_uses → returns false (trace: `sret-miss reason=O0-spill first_arg_reg=56`).

PART 1 (spill-following detect_sret) — DANGER, measured: 9 functions across 3 fixtures hit O0-spill sret-miss (cpp_rtti 1, debug_templates 1=make_array, debug_medium 7). CRITICALLY the 7 debug_medium functions (f_fill, f_array_sum, f_array_max, f_array_min, f_dot_product, f_linear_search, f_reduce) show spilled_to_stack=true BUT store_addr_uses=0, returned_through_ret=FALSE — they are NOT sret (real array-pointer args, return a scalar). A naive "spilled→sret" fix would FALSE-POSITIVE on all 7, corrupting their signatures. So part-1 must require: follow the spill slot's loads AND indirect-store-uses dominate AND the slot's value reaches RETURN. Only make_array (returned-through-rax) is genuine sret.

PART 2 (t61-COUPLED) — detect_sret runs at calling_conv_finalize.rs:248 AFTER final_params is computed and only RECORDS sret in FinalizedSignature; the c_printer signature renderer (lines ~1150/1582/1634) reads sig.params without special-casing sret (verified workspace-wide incl. byref path). So fixing detection alone removes ZERO phantom params. The phantom a2 is ALREADY dropped from the rendered sig (make_array(x)) but RESURFACES as an uninitialized body temp (`__int64 a2; // temp`) — the exact dropped-but-live-register leak-absorption that t61 owns.

DISTINCTION FROM t61: the sret pointer is RETURNED through rax (IR: RETURN v65549), unlike t61's non-returned loop cursor — so part-2 MIGHT be independently solvable (drop params[0] + retype return as the struct), but the leak-absorption still needs t61's mechanism. Keep blocked_by t61 conservatively; re-scope to unblock if part-2's leak-absorption proves independent. Needs: (a) precise spill-following detector excluding the 7 false-positives, (b) consumer drop+absorb hidden ptr, (c) leak-absorption [=t61], (d) DWARF return→Array<long,4> + fix DWARF formal mapping (x mapped to rdi=hidden ptr, also wrong).
t64.acceptance_criteria: UNLACE_CALLING_TRACE shows make_array sret result=true; make_array emits no phantom a2; the 7 debug_medium array-pointer functions are NOT mis-detected as sret; semantic-report 25/0; passes tests green; golden_fixtures count unchanged or improved; clippy -D warnings clean.

t61.subject: [blocked-deep] SSA/lvar live-range split for pointer/scalar register aliasing
t61.description:
DEEP BLOCKER — NOW REDUCED TO A WIRING STEP (verified this session). Baseline clean 25/0. Risk: High, effort: max — too broad for one turn (proven across ~17 measured-and-reverted attempts); execute as a dedicated session.

ROOT CAUSE (proven): the live-on-entry param fix (= t62+t63, atomic with this) surfaces register r9 aliasing a pointer cursor + a scalar collapsed under one C name → pointer-deref-of-scalar crash / runtime wrong-answer.

VALIDATED, REUSABLE BUILDING BLOCKS (all in docs/design-lvar-liverange-split-2026-06-01.md, updates a–q):
1. PARAM FIX (component 1, = t62/t63): collect_live_on_entry_reads in calling_convention.rs (backward CFG liveness; calls clobber arg regs; outgoing-call-arg operand reads excluded). Replaces the any-block read union. Proven correct.
2. classify_value_lattice (register_coalesce.rs): a monotonic, order-independent Unknown⊑{Pointer,Scalar}⊑Conflict value-class fixpoint with FORWARD (COPY/phi join) + BACKWARD (Pointer flows use→def) propagation. Hard seeds: Load/Store address operand=Pointer; mult/shift/div/rem/and/or/xor/zext/sext/subpiece output=Scalar. VALIDATED via UNLACE_LATTICE_DUMP — r9 classes are CORRECT (ZEXT digits=Scalar, pointer chain=Pointer; the earlier "v8 inversion" was a STALE-IR artifact, disproven by UNLACE_SEED_TRACE in update-q).
3. IV-protection (collect_iv_protected_versions from find_natural_loops + detect_basic_ivs) — keeps loop cursors whole.
4. string-based rendered_base_is_scalar printer guard (c_printer.rs, arrow + 3 subscript arms) — bails uncompilable scalar->field/scalar[i] to raw deref. Belt-and-suspenders.

THE MISSING STEP (update-q, the actual remaining work — NOT more analysis):
classify_value_lattice was BUILT + VALIDATED but NEVER WIRED into the split. partition_register_phases still classifies components by the OLD has_addr/has_arith use-site sets, which ARE inverted (that is why attempts #12-14 inverted r9's split). WIRE IT:
  a. In partition_register_phases, replace the has_addr/has_arith component classification with the lattice ValueClass: a component is Pointer/Scalar/Conflict per its members' lattice class.
  b. Union only same-class versions (a phi/COPY joining Pointer+Scalar is a SPLIT point, not a merge).
  c. Split: each register with a disjoint Pointer-web + Scalar-web (Conflict present, not IV-protected) → force the Scalar web to a fresh cN.
  d. Apply coupled with the param fix (1) + the printer guard (4).
  e. Validate: UNLACE_PART_DUMP shows correct webs (rsi/pointer vs ZEXT/scalar separated), then semantic-report 25/0, medium/stripped:main exit=33 (not crash/timeout), passes+output green, clippy clean. REVERT on any regression.

Each build is several minutes; this is iterative wiring+validation, hence a dedicated session. All prior reverts kept baseline 25/0.

t60.subject: Fix phantom argument over-detection inflating precision denominator
t60.description:

Root cause: `classify_variables` assigned `VarRole::Argument` to every arg-register read in the entry block (lines 270-277, 299-305, 350-353), regardless of whether the register index exceeded `inferred_params.len()`. - All gates green: passes 1157/1157, semantic-report 25/0, quality_smoke 7/7, clippy/fmt clean

t56.subject: [investigation] f_ackermann residual gotos — VERIFIED genuinely irreducible (no CFG bug)
t56.description:
RESOLVED via ground-truth tracing (commit fccaf7e60). Investigated whether f_ackermann's 16 residual gotos stem from a fixable CFG-construction bug. They do NOT. Two of my earlier hypotheses were WRONG and are now disproven by instrumentation:

1. WRONG (and fabricated-as-done earlier): "merge_linear_blocks won't merge call-terminated blocks." That edit never even applied (targeted wrong file). Calls are not the fragmentation driver.
2. WRONG: "7 unresolved CBRANCH targets / dropped edges." Added UNLACE_CFG_BUILD_TRACE to build_function_from_insns: f_ackermann builds 90 blocks / 90 leaders / ZERO dropped edges. The "c0x19f8"-style values in IR text are just the Const target operand every CBRANCH carries (normal pcode) — not missing edges.

VERIFIED ACTUAL CAUSE: f_ackermann's compiled CFG is genuinely irreducible. UNLACE_SPLIT_TRACE shows split_irreducible_entries detects ONE SCC of 68 body blocks with 22 distinct entry blocks (e.g. BB_36->BB_33, BB_47->BB_29, BB_50->BB_25 — branches into the middle of sibling chains). Tarjan SCC + >1-entry detection (irreducible.rs) is textbook-correct. node_split is correctly STUCK (every single-entry split is non-shrinking, largest_body stays 68, split_now=0 round 0 — raising MAX_SPLIT_ROUNDS cannot help). The double recursion was lowered by the compiler to a multi-entry state machine; the 16 gotos are HONEST output. The golden's goto-free form is IDA reconstructing semantics, not preserving this CFG.

DELIVERABLE: two reusable env-gated traces (UNLACE_CFG_BUILD_TRACE, UNLACE_SPLIT_TRACE), byte-identical-safe. The only path to fewer gotos here is DREAM multi-header/abnormal-entry structuring (separate active frontier, commits ...01d204384 nested-cyclic-decomposition), NOT a lifter/CFG fix. No code fix warranted; closing.
